A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ACC-MARL work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original TokenEnv experiments, policy ablations, task-assignment evaluations and qualitative rollouts in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including Table 1, training curves and appendix rollout analyses.

M1.justification: DFA progression, potential-based reward shaping, pretrained GATv2/RAD embeddings, shared IPPO policies and value-based task assignment are retained. The revised explanations and sampler pseudocode do not establish a changed implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Buttons-2, Rooms-2, Buttons-4 and Rooms-4 with Reach, ReachAvoid and RAD tasks, including larger out-of-distribution DFAs. Continuous domains and heterogeneous teams appear only as future directions in v2.

E2.justification: The same pretrained/untrained encoder, shaping/no-shaping and history-dependent LSTM comparisons remain. Table 1 retains the same two policy variants and assignment comparisons; newly cited methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported IPPO hyperparameters, 10-million-step budget, DFA-size limits and 1,000-episode evaluations are unchanged. Both retain uniform task-size sampling for policy training and geometric sampling for encoder pretraining; revised pseudocode does not establish a changed experimental setting.

E4.justification: The history-dependency, reward-shaping and embedding ablations, generalization tests, assignment analysis and cooperative behavior case studies are retained. Appendix Figures 8–14 contain the same analyses and traces.

E5.justification: Both report five random seeds, the same plus/minus reporting in Table 1 and standard-deviation bands in training plots. No uncertainty-estimation or statistical-testing procedure is added or changed.

E6.justification: All 96 numerical mean/plus-minus pairs in Table 1 match exactly. The corresponding training curves and qualitative rollout figures also retain their results, including the main plot renumbered from Figure 4 to Figure 3.

T1.justification: The retained optimality proof corrects the history/state alignment in Equation (8) and its transition kernel: v1 Appendix B.1 pairs s_(t+1) with A_t, while v2 Appendix A aligns s_t with A_t. Equation (5) now uses an explicit finite horizon, and Section 3.5 replaces the displayed success-probability inequality with a proxy-value inequality. The main theorem and proof strategy remain.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the multitask decentralized framework, optimality guarantees, value-based task assignment, JAX implementation and emergent cooperation. v2's explicit optimality wording restates guarantees already present in v1.

C2.justification: The new Discussion adds a DFA-expressivity rationale and qualifications concerning fixed task semantics, discrete-only validation and homogeneous cooperative teams. Existing full-observability and assignment-enumeration limitations are expanded, while interpretations of the experimental findings remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a separate TokenEnv code-access reference, explains that the DFA space is represented implicitly, and documents progression/minimization costs. Sampler pseudocode becomes more explicit about sequence lengths and accepting helper tasks; architecture and hyperparameter details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds fixed-specification MARL references by Hammond, Sun, Terashima and Paul, plus Sipser for DFA expressivity, and removes the Voloshin reference. These expand the supporting context while retaining the central positioning around formal specifications for multitask MARL.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten, Section 4 is condensed and its detailed implementation material moves to Appendix B. The proof becomes Appendix A, limitations are integrated into a new Discussion, and acknowledgements and an impact statement are added.

P2.justification: v2 adopts an ICML-style layout with revised typography, headers, captions and single-column appendices. Four-agent environment panels move from main-text Figure 3 to appendix Figure 6, the additional RAD example panel is removed, and existing figures, tables and algorithms are resized or repositioned.

improvement.justification: Corrected proof indexing, clearer implementation and access information, and more explicit applicability limits improve precision and transparency. These are useful but limited gains: the core method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
